verses.1: And there will be no way out for the children of Israel from their bonds and restrictions.
verses.2: And the LORD said to Joshua, “See, I have given you Jericho and its king, along with all the nobles of the city.”
verses.3: And they destroyed the city. All the soldiers who were fighting in that city attacked the city once. Do this for six days.
verses.4: And seven priests will carry seven trumpets, which are used before the altar. On the seventh day, they will blow the trumpets seven times. The priests will then strike the trumpets with their hands.
verses.5: And in the evening, as you heard the sound of the trumpet, all the people cried out in great sorrow. The heart of the city was broken, and the people rose up against each other.
verses.6: And Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Bring forward the Ark of the Covenant.” Seventy priests carried seven baskets filled with offerings before the Ark of God.
verses.7: And he said to the people, “Go forward and turn around the city. Let the river flow before the presence of Jehovah.”
verses.8: And it was said by Joshua to the people. Seven priests carried seven trumpets before Jehovah. They blew the trumpets, and the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah followed behind them.
verses.9: And the Levites went ahead of the priests, who were carrying the trumpets. The people followed behind them, and they kept playing the trumpets as they moved along.
verses.10: And Joshua commanded the people, “Do not make any noise or shout loudly. No word shall come out of your mouths until I say to you, ‘Shout!’ Then you may shout.”
verses.11: And the Ark of God moved through the city once. Then they entered the camp, and they slept in the camp.
verses.12: And Yehoshua ascended into the sky in the morning. Then the priests carried the Ark of God.
verses.13: And seven priests carry seven trumpets, which are placed in front of the Ark of God. They walk forward, and they blow the trumpets. The wind then blows ahead of them. And the collection of people walks behind the Ark of God. They also blow the trumpets.
verses.14: On the second day, they captured the city once again. They stayed there for six days.
verses.15: And on the seventh day, they gathered together as black as night. They destroyed the city seven times over, just on that day. They destroyed the city seven times in total.
verses.16: And on the seventh day, the priests struck the trumpets. Yehoshua said to the people, “May the Lord give you this city.”
verses.17: And it shall be a city of destruction. All those who are in it will die. Only those who are in the house will survive, since they have hidden the messengers that we sent.
verses.18: And only you shall keep away from the punishment. Do not take part in it, and do not allow anyone to take part in it. Instead, make sure that Israel’s camp is protected from such punishment.
verses.19: And all silver and gold, as well as all other precious metals and bronze, are sacred to Jehovah. They belong to Jehovah’s treasure.
verses.20: The people became angry, and they rushed into the streets. When the people heard the sound of the trumpets, they became extremely furious. The city was filled with chaos. The people rushed towards the city, and one man stood against them and captured the city.
verses.21: And they destroyed everything that was in the city, from men to women, from young people to old people, from slaves to servants, and from priests to Levites.
verses.22: And to those two men who were driving the land, Joshua said, “Go into the house of the woman. Take her and all those who belong to her with you, as they promised to give them to her.”
verses.23: And the young men who were riding on the donkeys came and brought out her father, her mother, her brothers, and all those who belonged to her. They also brought out all her relatives. Then they set them aside, outside the camp of Israel.
verses.24: And the city was burned down by fire. All that was in it was destroyed: only the gold and silver, along with all kinds of precious objects and metals, were saved as treasures for the house of Jehovah.
verses.25: And the land of Canaan, and her father’s house, and all that belonged to her, Joshua took over. She remained in Israel until today. This is because she hid the idols that Joshua had sent to be destroyed.
verses.26: And Joshua said at that time, “May the name of this man be blessed before Jehovah. For he will build and establish this city, and make it a place of peace.”
verses.27: And Jehovah made Jehosua, and he became king throughout all the land.
